findings.quote: Removing $t$ from the two position equations gives a **parabola**.
findings.problem: Stated as a general result of the ideal model, but it fails at the boundary $v_{x0}=0$. A ball dropped or thrown straight up moves along a vertical straight line, not a parabola (and $t$ cannot be removed through $x=x_0$). The lesson names both exceptions itself: the bullet just above cites 'a ball dropped from the same height', and The Highest Point section cites 'a ball thrown straight up'. A student asked for the path of a ball thrown vertically upward gets 'parabola' from this sentence. The base had the same unqualified sentence; the round-1 read did not raise it.
findings.source: Checklist B01; reader rules, Added after the Sol audit (boundary test); OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, 4.3 Projectile Motion, trajectory equation $y=(\tan\theta_0)x-\dfrac{g}{2(v_0\cos\theta_0)^2}x^2$, which is undefined at $\theta_0=90^\circ$

findings.quote: For example, at the bottom of a swing, $T-mg=mv^2/r$.
findings.problem: The symbol $T$ is never defined as tension. Earlier the lesson defines $T$ as the total flight time, and later it defines $T$ as the period; Example #7 writes tension as $F_T$. The one equation that shows how to subtract an outward force part uses a symbol whose only meaning so far is a time, so the student cannot read the rule without guessing.
findings.source: Checklist L25 (symbols explained before their meanings are needed); LSG Teaching completeness

findings.quote: When you solve, first find the center. Then take each real force along the line to the center.
findings.problem: This paragraph has six sentences, above the one-to-three limit. The friction paragraph just before it has five.
